vocabulary.definition: a device used in microwave ovens to generate microwaves
vocabulary.example: The microwave oven operates by emitting microwaves produced by the magnetron.

vocabulary.definition: relating to the force that resists the relative motion or tendency to such motion of two bodies in contact
vocabulary.example: The microwaves cause frictional heat in the food molecules, heating them up quickly.

vocabulary.definition: moving back and forth in a regular rhythm
vocabulary.example: The oscillating electric and magnetic fields of light energy create waves of varying frequencies.

vocabulary.definition: causing atoms to lose or gain electrons, resulting in the formation of ions
vocabulary.example: High-frequency, ionizing radiation can be harmful to human cells by altering their DNA.

vocabulary.definition: an ionized gas consisting of positive ions and free electrons in proportions resulting in no overall electrical charge
vocabulary.example: When high voltages are reached, the electrically charged gas, or plasma, may form lightning-like sparks.

vocabulary.definition: not level, flat, or smooth, causing disparities or irregularities
vocabulary.example: Metal objects in the microwave might make food cook unevenly due to the concentration of electrons at sharp edges.
